stem:
The properties of chlorine, bromine and their compounds are compared.
Which property is smaller for chlorine than for bromine?

options.A: bond strength of the hydrogen-halide bond
options.C: solubility of the silver halide in NH₃(aq)
options.D: strength of the van der Waals’ forces between molecules of the element

stem: Why do the halogens become less volatile as Group 17 is descended?

options.C: The number of electrons in each molecule increases.
options.D: The van der Waals’ forces between molecules become weaker.

stem:
X, Y and Z are three elements in Group 17.
X₂ has weaker covalent bonds than Y₂.
X₂ has stronger instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces between its molecules than Z₂.
Y₂ is a stronger oxidising agent than Z₂.
What could be X, Y and Z?
X
Y

When descending Group 17 from chlorine to iodine, which statement is correct?

options.A: The hydrides become less thermally stable as they become weaker reducing agents.
options.B: The hydrides become more thermally stable as the reactivity of the elements decreases.
options.C: The volatility of the elements decreases as the van der Waals’ forces increase.
options.D: The volatility of the elements increases as the size of the molecules increases.

stem:
The volatility of the Group 17 elements, chlorine, bromine and iodine, decreases down the group.
What is responsible for this trend?

options.A: bond length in the halogen molecule
options.B: bond strength in the halogen molecule
options.D: number of electrons in the halogen atom

stem: Which property explains the trend in volatility of the elements going down Group 17?
Which statement explains why iodine is less volatile than chlorine?

options.A: Chlorine is more electronegative than iodine and so has more repulsion between its molecules.
options.B: The greater number of electrons in iodine leads to larger temporary dipole-induced dipole forces.
options.C: The I–I bond energy is smaller than the Cl –Cl bond energy.
options.D: The iodine molecules have stronger permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces.

stem:
In this question, Q represents an atom of chlorine, bromine or iodine.
Which explanation for the variation in volatility down Group 17 is correct?
Instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces between molecules become stronger.

options.A: Permanent dipole–permanent dipole forces between molecules become stronger.
options.B: The bond energy of the Q₂ molecules decreases.
options.C: The first ionisation energy Q(g) →Q⁺(g) + e⁻ decreases.

stem:
Iodine has a higher melting point than chlorine.
What is the reason for this?
Iodine has stronger covalent bonds than chlorine.

options.A: Iodine molecules have stronger permanent dipoles than chlorine molecules.
options.B: Iodine is more volatile than chlorine.
options.C: Iodine has stronger instantaneous dipole–induced dipole forces than chlorine.
